correctness.rationale: For one Bell-pair block a selected subsystem retains 0/1/2 endpoints and contributes purity 1,1/2,1; selecting one endpoint has combinatorial multiplicity 2. Hence the contribution after weighting by purity has local polynomial 1+x+x², proving mean m-subsystem purity [x^m](1+x+x²)^K/binom(2K,m). For m=K, the coefficient is the central trinomial T_K∼sqrt(3)3^K/(2sqrt(pi K)), while binom(2K,K)∼4^K/sqrt(pi K), yielding sqrt(3)/2(3/4)^K. The ratio to 2^-K grows as (3/2)^K and Scott Q_K tends to 1; K≥2 states factor into entangled two-qubit blocks and have depth 2. Independently enumerated K≤8 subsets; the asymptotic follows analytically, not from finite enumeration.

Prior de Oliveira–Rigolin work already points out that Bell-pair products can lack genuine multipartite entanglement despite high global-entanglement values, so that qualitative point is not counted as new.
